key_insight: AVGen-Bench introduces a task-driven, multi-granular benchmark that evaluates text-to-audio-video (T2AV) systems on fine‑grained joint correctness, not just isolated or coarse embedding similarity.
problem_solved: Current evaluations treat audio and video separately or rely on coarse embedding scores, missing semantic, temporal and cross-modal details needed to judge whether a generated audio-video pair truly matches realistic text prompts.
method: Curate a high-quality prompt suite spanning 11 real-world categories to reflect diverse, realistic T2AV requests.
Define a multi-granular evaluation protocol that breaks joint correctness into layered criteria (e.g., semantic alignment, temporal synchronization, local-detail fidelity and cross-modal coherence).
Provide an assessment workflow (automated metrics + task-driven checks and human-readable categories) to measure performance at each granularity and enable fair comparison across models.
impact: AVGen-Bench gives researchers and engineers a standardized, fine-grained way to measure and debug T2AV models, enabling more meaningful progress and model selection for real-world audio-video generation tasks.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: text prompt → model → generated audio+video with annotated evaluation checkpoints (semantic, temporal, local detail).
Multi-panel example grid: for several prompts show ground truth (if applicable) vs. model outputs with per-granularity scores.
Radar/spider chart: compare models across evaluation axes (semantic alignment, sync, audio quality, visual fidelity, cross-modal coherence).
Timeline visualization: highlight temporal misalignments between audio events and visual frames for failure analysis.
paper_title: AVGen-Bench: A Task-Driven Benchmark for Multi-Granular Evaluation of Text-to-Audio-Video Generation
paper_authors: Ziwei Zhou, Zeyuan Lai, Rui Wang, Yifan Yang, Zhen Xing
